summary: The Sackler family, owners of Purdue Pharma, launched OxyContin in 1996 and marketed it to American doctors as barely addictive, fuelling the opioid epidemic while earning billions and dodging personal blame.

evidence.note: Arthur Sackler buys Purdue Frederick in 1952; covered span starts here
Arthur pioneers medical journal advertising, then sells Valium via invented psychic tension
OxyContin launched; Richard's blizzard of prescriptions speech
executives and Richard agree not to correct doctors' belief it is weaker than morphine
war on pain: funded advocacy groups and pain as fifth vital sign
overdose deaths, grieving mothers' meeting and letter about a dead son
short segment on trying to have OxyContin decontrolled in Germany
sales force, junkets, prescriber targeting and coupons for first-time users
2007 Virginia case: three executives plead guilty, family shielded
Richard and Beth Sackler Foundation gifts to Islamophobic groups
2019 Oklahoma settlement and New York suit bring story to release

notes: Primary subject is the family as a group, so the lifetime rule does not apply; covered span starts with the 1952 Purdue purchase, the immigrant grandparents being a brief mention. main_span end null as Purdue and the family were active and in litigation at release. Germany segment is about 3 minutes, so DE left out of setting. journalist-propagandist role reflects the family's marketing focus; no exact role for pharma marketers.
